name: Reissner-Nordstrom: Misner-Sharp mass m(r) = M - Q^2/2r, energy density rho = Q^2/8 pi r^4 > 0 -- the counterexample to the COROLLARY

source.located: Classics: H. Reissner, Annalen der Physik 355 (1916) 106; G. Nordstrom, Verh. Koninkl. Ned. Akad. Wet. 26 (1918) 1201; C. W. Misner & D. H. Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136 (1964) B571 (Misner-Sharp mass). No arXiv copies exist. Read through exact restatements: (a) S. M. Carroll, 'Lecture Notes on General Relativity', arXiv:gr-qc/9712019, section 7 eq. (7.106)-(7.113) and pp. 201-206 (the RN metric, F_tr = -q/r^2, T_munu = (1/4 pi)(F F - g F^2/4), horizons r_pm, timelike singularity, the three cases); (b) S. A. Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', arXiv:gr-qc/9408002, eq. (4) [E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)), G = 1], eq. (27) ['the form actually given by Misner & Sharp'], eq. (28a) [E' = 4 pi r^2 (T_00 r' - T_01 rdot)], the regular-centre definition (E = O(r^3)), Proposition 2 (a central singularity with E < 0 is temporal and untrapped), Proposition 6 (DEC + untrapped hypersurface + regular centre => E >= 0) and the remark 'E may be negative, as in the negative-energy Schwarzschild solution'; (c) S. Jalalzadeh & H. Moradpour, arXiv:2602.22559, eq. (1)-(5): M_MSH(r) = (r/2G)(1 - f(r)) = m - q^2/(2r) for RN under 'the standard Einstein-Maxwell normalization', and section 4 on the static Killing vector changing causal character across the horizons; (d) N. R. Ghosh & M. K. Nandy, arXiv:2412.14618, eq. (1) with references [2],[3] naming Reissner 1916 and Nordstrom 1918 by title.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9712019, gr-qc/9408002, 2602.22559 and 2412.14618 (page text read; every quotation below is from those pages). Reissner 1916, Nordstrom 1918 and Misner-Sharp 1964 themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ; the RN metric, its field and stress tensor, and the Misner-Sharp definition are read in the restatements, and the combined statement m_MS(RN) = M - Q^2/2r is READ verbatim in 2602.22559 eq. (5).

published_statement: Carroll (7.110)-(7.113): ds^2 = -Delta dt^2 + Delta^{-1} dr^2 + r^2 dOmega^2, Delta = 1 - 2GM/r + G(p^2 + q^2)/r^2, 'M is once again interpreted as the mass of the hole; q is the total electric charge, and p is the total magnetic charge'; F_tr = -q/r^2, F_thetaphi = p sin theta; T_munu = (1/4 pi)(F_murho F_nu^rho - g_munu F_rhosigma F^rhosigma / 4); 'at r = 0 there is a true curvature singularity'; r_pm = GM pm sqrt(G^2 M^2 - G(p^2 + q^2)); for GM^2 > p^2 + q^2 'the singularity at r = 0 is a timelike line'; for GM^2 < p^2 + q^2 'the mass of the matter which carried the charge would have had to be negative'. Hayward eq. (4): E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)) in units G = 1; eq. (27): 1 - 2E/r = e^{-lambda} r'^2 - rdot^2, 'the form actually given by Misner & Sharp'; a centre is regular iff g^{-1}(dr,dr) - 1 = O(r^2), 'then E = O(r^3) at a regular centre'; eq. (28a): E' = 4 pi r^2 (T_00 r' - T_01 rdot); Prop. 6: 'If the dominant energy condition holds on an untrapped spatial hypersurface with regular centre, then E >= 0'; 'Note first that E may be negative, as in the negative-energy Schwarzschild solution'; Prop. 2: 'A central singularity is spatial and trapped if E > 0, and temporal and untrapped if E < 0'. Jalalzadeh-Moradpour eq. (5): M_MSH(r) = (r/2G)(1 - g^{ab} nabla_a r nabla_b r) = (r/2G)(1 - f(r)) = m - q^2/(2r), with f = 1 - 2Gm/r + Gq^2/r^2 and p_i = q^2/(8 pi r_i^4) as 'the local electromagnetic energy density'.
published_hypotheses: Einstein-Maxwell equations G_ab = 8 pi T_ab (G = c = 1) with the Maxwell stress tensor in Gaussian normalisation T = (1/4 pi)(F F - g F^2/4) (Carroll (7.107); Jalalzadeh-Moradpour footnote 1 'standard Einstein-Maxwell normalization')
spherical symmetry; the static form is a consequence (Carroll derives it under the general spherically symmetric ansatz (7.106))
asymptotic flatness fixing the integration constant as the ADM mass M; charge q (and optionally magnetic charge p) fixed by Gauss's law at infinity
Misner-Sharp energy defined geometrically on spheres, E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)), no matter assumption (Hayward eq. (4))

first law dE = 4 pi r^2 (T_00 r' - T_01 rdot) needs the Einstein equations (Hayward (28a)); positivity E >= 0 needs in addition the dominant energy condition, an untrapped spatial hypersurface AND a regular centre E = O(r^3) (Hayward Prop. 6)
the source itself records that E can be negative when the regular-centre hypothesis fails ('negative-energy Schwarzschild solution', Hayward p. 8-9)
hypothesis_drift: certify.py:138 states rho = Q^2/8 pi r^4 and m = M - Q^2/2r with NO unit convention for Q; the source is Gaussian with G = c = 1 (Carroll (7.107)-(7.111)). In Heaviside-Lorentz both would read Q^2/4 pi. The region r < Q^2/2M and every conclusion are convention-covariant (Q^2 rescales identically in m and rho), so this is a discrepancy of statement, not of result. drivensource.py and tolman.py:437 do state 'G = c = 1, Gaussian', and drivensource.py:348-351's SI form X = Q^2/(8 pi eps0 c^2) is the correct SI translation of the Gaussian Q^2/2 (verified: 5.0000000027e-08 kg m per C^2).

The source carries magnetic charge p alongside q (p^2 + q^2 everywhere); the tree uses electric Q only (all owners). Narrower, and harmless: every statement survives Q^2 -> p^2 + q^2 (tolman.py:462 already names 'magnetic monopole').

The tree's 'rho > 0 everywhere' (certify.py:138, drivensource.py:118, overturn.py:45, throatmass.py:45) is the static-frame density -T^t_t; the static Killing vector is spacelike between r_- and r_+ (2602.22559 section 4; Carroll p. 204), where no static observer exists. The rederivation section C shows T(u,u) = rho (1 + 2A) with A >= 0 for EVERY unit timelike u using only the normalisation, so the claim holds observer-independently in every region. A gap the tree leaves unstated, closed here; no drift against the source.

tolman.py:441-443 (V13) and drivensource.py:94-98 obtain the RN mass function by solving the Misner-Sharp equations with the electrovac source and then MATCH to the metric function, which the tree itself labels 'matched to, not derived'. Section A of the rederivation derives the metric from Einstein-Maxwell with an undetermined f(r), h(r): Maxwell gives q = C sqrt(f/h)/r^2, G^t_t = G^r_r forces f = h, G^t_t = 8 pi T^t_t integrates to h = 1 + C1/r + Q^2/r^2 with C1 = -2M, and all remaining components vanish. The hypothesis 'the RN metric is the standard exterior solution' is therefore discharged, not assumed.

specthm.py:570-571 (H_EFE) uses only the tt component dm/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho; Hayward's (28a) is stated for a spatial hypersurface with T_00 the density seen by its normal. Applied by the tree both outside r_+ and inside r_- (static regions) and implicitly everywhere: verified here as an identity of the mixed components G^t_t = 8 pi T^t_t on RN at every r, so the use is sound.

tolman.py:470-474 'The region R < Q^2/(2M) lies STRICTLY INSIDE the inner (Cauchy) horizon for every 0 < Q <= M': true for each fixed Q (gap = (1 - sqrt(1 - y))^2 / 2 > 0, exact identity, and z3-unsat negation), but not uniform -- r_c/r_- = (1 + sqrt(1 - q^2))/2 -> 1 as q -> 0+. drivensource.py:366-368 writes the ratio as <= 1, which is the exact statement. Recorded; nothing in the tree rests on uniformity.

The containment inside r_- depends on Q <= M (Gibbons-Hull/Witten, a separate audited result, invoked at charge.py:28-30 and drivensource.py:166-169). For Q > M there is no horizon and z3 confirms Q^2/(2M) > M/2 always: the m < 0 region would be naked. The tree does not drop this hypothesis; it is named. No drift.

specthm.py:896-897 / drivensource.py:129-131 / V6 label m(0+) = -infinity as 'a -infinite bare mass at the point charge'. The limit is computed (sympy, here and at drivensource.py:532-533); the words 'bare mass' are an interpretation of the integration constant that no source states. Hayward's own counterexample for a missing regular centre is negative-mass Schwarzschild (vacuum, E constant < 0); RN sharpens it (DEC-satisfying matter, E -> -infinity). An interpretive label, not a drift in a hypothesis.

rederivation.outcome: 54 checks, all PASS, exit 0, 4.7 s (sympy 1.14.0, z3 5.1.0). A: RN DERIVED from Einstein-Maxwell with undetermined f(r), h(r): Maxwell => q = C sqrt(f/h)/r^2; T^t_t = T^r_r => G^t_t - G^r_r = h'/r - h f'/(r f) = 0 => f = C h; G^t_t = 8 pi T^t_t => h = 1 + C1/r + Q^2/r^2, C1 = -2M; every component of G^a_b - 8 pi T^a_b vanishes on RN; T traceless. B: E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)) = M - Q^2/(2r) by Hayward's definition; rho = -T^t_t = Q^2/(8 pi r^4), p_r = -rho, p_t = +rho; dm/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho; conservation; m = 0 exactly at r = Q^2/(2M); m < 0 on (0, 8/25) at M = 1, Q = 4/5; m(0+) = -oo; int_0^R 4 pi r^2 rho dr = oo; m - 4 pi r^3 p_r = M at every r; Kretschmann = 48 M^2/r^6 - 96 M Q^2/r^7 + 56 Q^4/r^8 (true singularity). C: T(u,u) = rho (1 + 2A), A >= 0, for every unit timelike u from the normalisation alone -- positive in every region; DEC holds with equality. D: h(r_pm) = 0; gap series y^2/8 + y^3/16 and exact form (1 - sqrt(1-y))^2/2; r_c/r_- = (1 + sqrt(1-q^2))/2, = 1/2 at q = 1, -> 1 as q -> 0; tolman.py's M = 1, Q = 0.8 table (0.32; 0.4, 1.6) exact; drivensource.py:555-557 and charge.py:16-24 tables reproduced; SI X = 5.0e-08 kg m per C^2 under CODATA 2018 and 2022; electron r_c = 1.4090e-15 m = r_e/2; the 0.4999848 shell ratio. E (z3): E1 'm < 0 <=> 2MR < Q^2' negation unsat with both sat guards; Q^2/(2M) <= r_- for 0 < Q <= M negation unsat, strict case sat; Q > M => Q^2/2M > M/2 (naked); observer-positivity unsat negation. F: Hayward Prop. 2 consistent -- E < 0 and h -> +oo at the centre (untrapped), trapped region exactly (r_-, r_+). later_literature.ref: S. A. Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', arXiv:gr-qc/9408002 (1994, rev. 1995), Phys. Rev. D 53, 1938
later_literature.what: The Misner-Sharp energy is geometric (eq. 4); E = O(r^3) at a regular centre; positivity (Prop. 6) needs DEC + untrapped hypersurface + REGULAR CENTRE, and the paper states outright that E may be negative without it. RN satisfies DEC (verified) and fails only the regular centre -- so the tree's narrowing of certify.py's corollary to m(0) = 0 is exactly the source's own hypothesis, and RN is a sharper witness than the source's (vacuum negative-mass Schwarzschild). Prop. 2 (E < 0 central singularity is temporal, untrapped) agrees with Carroll's 'r = 0 is a timelike line'.

later_literature.what: Eq. (5) states M_MSH(r) = m - q^2/(2r) for RN verbatim under the standard Einstein-Maxwell normalisation, with p = q^2/(8 pi r^4) the local electromagnetic energy density (eq. 8); section 4 records that the static Killing vector is spacelike between the horizons (the caveat behind the tree's 'rho > 0 everywhere', closed observer-independently in the rederivation).

Nandy, 'Nonlinear Dynamics of the Inner Horizon in Reissner-Nordstrom Black Holes', arXiv:2412.14618 (2024)
later_literature.what: The exact RN interior inside r_- is unstable: under generic perturbation the mass function m(v) diverges at the Cauchy horizon (Poisson-Israel; Ori 1991; Ghosh-Nandy find the inner horizon shrinks rho(v) -> 0 and m(v) = Q^2/(2 rho) - m_0 -> +infinity). Since the tree's m < 0 region r < Q^2/2M lies inside r_- for every Q <= M, no perturbed physical charged black hole realises it, and where it would sit the Misner-Sharp mass inflates to +infinity, the opposite sign. This narrows only a DEVICE reading, which the tree already refuses: tolman.py:473 'RN IS A WITNESS ABOUT HYPOTHESES, NOT A DEVICE', phase1.py:405-407 Lambda = 0.0, charge.py:32 'inside its matter, not in a corridor'. The mathematical counterexample to the corollary -- an exact static spherically symmetric Einstein-Maxwell solution with m < 0 and rho > 0 -- is untouched by stability.

lacked_data: What Reissner (1916) and Nordstrom (1918) had: Einstein's equations, Maxwell's theory and Schwarzschild's solution; what they lacked: the horizon structure and maximal extension (Graves-Brill 1960, Carter 1966), the Misner-Sharp mass (1964), the Cauchy-horizon instability (Simpson-Penrose 1973, Poisson-Israel 1989), the positive-energy theorem for Einstein-Maxwell (Gibbons-Hull 1982, Witten) bounding Q <= M, and any observation of a charged black hole (still none). Evidence FOR M's hypothesis: later data do change the physical reading of the r < Q^2/2M region -- it sits inside a Cauchy horizon that mass inflation destroys, where the perturbed mass function goes to +infinity, and inside the matter of any charged body -- so the classical picture of a static negative-mass core is not what a physical charged object contains. Evidence AGAINST it for THIS result: the statement the tree rests on is an exact solution of the field equations and an algebraic identity of its metric, re-derived here with no empirical input at all (section A derives the metric, section B computes the mass by definition); no datum enters, so no later datum can move it, and the conclusion drawn from it -- that 'm < 0 => negative enclosed energy' needs the regular-centre hypothesis m(0) = 0 -- is a theorem about the equation dm/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho, which Hayward's Proposition 6 states with that very hypothesis. The later data restrict what RN may be used FOR (not a device), a restriction every owner already applies.
grade_evidence: (1) The statement as used -- m = M - Q^2/(2r), rho = Q^2/(8 pi r^4) > 0, m < 0 iff r < Q^2/(2M), m(0+) = -oo, r_pm, the containment inside r_- for Q <= M -- is READ in exact restatements (Carroll (7.110)-(7.113); Hayward (4), (27), (28a); 2602.22559 eq. (5)) and agrees with every owner's text. (2) Re-derived from the Einstein-Maxwell equations with no assumed metric and the Misner-Sharp mass computed by its definition: 54/54 checks pass, including the z3 obligation E1 with satisfiability guards and the Cauchy-horizon containment as an unsat negation in nonlinear real arithmetic. (3) The hypotheses the tree names (static, spherical, pure electrovac, Gaussian G = c = 1, no regular centre, Q <= M for the containment) match the source's; the one hypothesis the source carries that the tree drops -- a regular centre for positivity -- is exactly the one the tree's use is ABOUT, and it drops it deliberately (D4 THEOREM: 'a hypothesis that was always in force and was unwritten'). (4) No datum enters the geometric statement; the SI translation moves by 7e-10 between CODATA 2018 and 2022 and the tree's 1e-9 pin passes under both. (5) Discrepancies recorded, none a refutation: certify.py:138 omits the unit convention; 'rho > 0 everywhere' is stated for the static frame and holds observer-independently (shown here, not in the tree); 'STRICTLY INSIDE' the Cauchy horizon is per-Q, not uniform; 'bare mass' is a label. (6) Later literature (mass inflation) narrows only a device reading the tree already refuses. Each owner's own selftest (drivensource, throatmass, tolman) exits 0 as it stands.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: any owner beginning to use the r < Q^2/2M region as a reachable region of a physical spacetime (a device), since mass inflation replaces the RN interior and there the Misner-Sharp mass goes to +infinity; or a use of the corollary's narrowing outside pure electrovac spherical symmetry (charged fluids, nonlinear electrodynamics), which drivensource.SCOPE already excludes. To WRONG: a computed contradiction in the identity E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)) = M - Q^2/2r or in dm/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho for RN -- none is possible, both are shown symbolically here -- or an inconsistent unit mixture in an owner (Heaviside-Lorentz rho against Gaussian m) that changed a stated region; the omission at certify.py:138 does not, because every figure there is Gaussian-consistent. To DATA-DEPENDENT: nothing -- no measured quantity enters the geometric statement, and the SI translation depends only on eps0 and c, both stable to 1e-9.
